prior_importants.description: The remedy the amendment gives for reopening an abandoned PR (`pup merge <session> --pr`) is refused by planRegate whenever the PR head did not move, and its message says to merge on GitHub and `pup land`. The freed ADR number then lands twice without any check.

`pup land --abandon-closed` treats a `MergeLockLostError` like any other refusal. If the lock is lost, the operator is never told that the `pr_closed` event was already written and the PR's ADR numbers are already freed. `pup land` and `pup retire` report what happened before they fail on a lost lock.

The `isClosedOut` and `competingBranches` JSDocs say a `pup land` that read the PR CLOSED records the close. A plain `pup land` of a CLOSED PR refuses and records nothing; only the operator's `pup land --abandon-closed` writes `pr_closed`.

findings.description: After `--abandon-closed` and a reopen on GitHub, a plain `pup land` tells the operator to "merge it there first". The PR is open with its head still at the pin, so following that advice merges it with no ADR-number re-check. A number a peer took after the record then reaches the target twice.
findings.body:
**Reopened abandoned PR: `pup land` tells the operator to merge with no ADR re-check**

The amended decision 146 relies on the operator re-gating a reopened, abandoned PR with `pup merge <session> --pr` before merging it. This PR changed `planRegate` so that, with the close on record, it re-gates an unmoved head (`pr.head === pinned && !merge.closedOnRecord`) instead of answering "Merge it on GitHub, then run `pup land`". `landSession` still gives that same advice on the same path:

```ts
if (pr.state !== 'MERGED') {
  throw new Error(
    `${prUrl} is ${sanitizeReason(pr.state ?? 'in an unreadable state')} on GitHub, not ` +
      'MERGED; merge it there first. Nothing was landed.',
  );
}
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/fceab2170a218af077360d86e8320fd7b8e7e4a4/src/core/land.service.ts#L119-L124

**Trigger.**
1. `pup land s --abandon-closed` records `pr_closed`, and `isClosedOut` drops `s` from `competingBranches`, which frees its ADR numbers.
2. A peer is gated with one of those numbers, and its PR merges.
3. The operator reopens `s`'s PR on GitHub. Its head is still at the pin.
4. The operator runs `pup land s`. The moved-head refusal (L102) needs `pr.head !== sha`, and the new CLOSED refusal (L111) needs `CLOSED`, so neither fires. Execution reaches L119: "is OPEN on GitHub, not MERGED; merge it there first."
5. The gate's success status on the pinned sha is still on GitHub, so the merge goes through. `newestMerge` skips `pr_closed`, so the next `pup land` lands it.

Result: two decisions under one number on the target. The ADR amendment rejects an unmoved-head refusal that "would send the operator to merge on GitHub and `pup land` with no check". That case is why `planRegate` changed, and this message is the same steer on the land side.

**Fix.** Before L119, refuse an OPEN PR whose close is on record and point the operator to the re-gate. `isPrClosedOnRecord` is already imported here, and `id` is the sanitized id in scope. Add a test that seeds `pr_closed` and fakes gh `OPEN` at the pin.

findings.description: `landablePullRequest`'s JSDoc sentence is garbled ("a PR of the repo origin was recorded as, pinned onto a target the gate's way"). Its refusals all end "Nothing was landed.", but `--abandon-closed` reaches them too, and it records rather than lands, so its other refusals say "Nothing was recorded."

`planRegate`'s JSDoc says "only a new merge event, which the ADR-number stage checks first, makes them its own again". The stage runs before that merge event exists, since the passing gate writes it. The ADR wording is accurate: the stage re-checks the numbers, and only its passing merge event makes them count again.

The `{ prUrl: string; recorded: boolean }` shape is written out inline three times: the CLI declaration, the `error.result` cast, and `abandonClosedSession`'s return type. `docs/conventions/general.md` §Code layout wants a reused type named in a types file, the way `LandOutcome` lives in `src/core/types/land.types.ts`.
